newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MSRB elects 5 new members for 3-yr terms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MSRB elects 5 new members for 3-yr terms.

text.p: The Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board announced Tuesday that it has elected five new members to serve three-year terms beginning Oct. 1.

The board has a total of 15 members -- five representatives of dealer banks, five of securities firms, and five public members not associated with any bank dealer or securities firm. At least one public member must represent issuers and one investors.

The new members include Howard Curlett III, managing director and president of First Union Capital Markets Corp.; Robert Estrada, chairman and CEO of Estrada Hinojosa & Co Inc., an investment banking firm that he founded in 1990; and James Fitzgerald, managing director for Banc One Capital Corp., in charge of municipal bond activities.

Also elected to the board were Thomas Kenny, senior vice president of Franklin Advisers, Inc. and director of Franklin's Municipal Bond Department; and Thomas Stanberry, managing director and director of fixed income capital markets for Piper Jaffray, Inc.

Curlett is responsible for administration of First Union's Section 20 broker-dealer as well public finance and municipal bond trading and sales. Before joining First Union, he was with J.P. Morgan & Co. for 21 years, including a stint as head of public finance.
Before launching Estrada Hinojosa, Estrada served as special assistant to former President George Bush and was a bond lawyer.
Fitzgerald, meanwhile, started Fitzgerald, Davis & Associates in 1993. The firm recently was acquired by Banc One.

Fitzgerald held senior positions with Kemper Securities, Inc.; Blunt Ellis & Loewi; and Paine Webber. He was chair of the National Association of Securities Dealers' District Eight Business Conduct Committee and NASD's national fixed income commmittee.

Stanberry is responsible for public finance, municipal, corporate and government underwriting and trading, and institutional sales at Piper Jaffray. Before joining the firm in 1989, he was was a bond attory for 10 years in Des Moines, Iowa.
